mainTopic: Husband and wife, then the haircut rules for the king and the כהנים, and why long hair and wine are treated differently today.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a story about רב יהודה's wife, who was quick to anger but quick to make peace. Next, רב teaches that a woman truly bonds with her first husband, and a ברייתא teaches that a death is felt most by the surviving spouse. The גמרא then returns to the משנה about the king's haircut and brings a ברייתא with three schedules: a מלך cuts his hair daily, a כהן גדול weekly, and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days. The thirty days is learned from נזיר through the shared word פרע, and the נזיר's thirty days comes from the גימטריא of יהיה. The גמרא asks why כהנים do not keep this rule today, and compares long hair to wine, which is forbidden only when entering the מקדש. This leads to a back-and-forth about why the רבנן forbid wine today but not long hair. רב אשי's answer is that a drunk כהן ruins the עבודה while a long-haired one does not, and it survives a challenge once the law is shown to be an old tradition that יחזקאל attached to a פסוק. The פרק ends by describing the special haircut of the כהנים and the כהן גדול.

steps.title: רב יהודה points to his own wife as the joyful 'wife of your youth'
steps.stepSummary: The story from the previous lines ends. רב יהודה had read his son the פסוק about rejoicing in 'the wife of your youth.' His son asked who fits that description, and רב יהודה answered: your mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: '...of your youth.' His son asked him: Like whom? He answered him: Like your mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes a story that started just before this point. רב יהודה gives his own wife as an example of a wife who brings her husband joy.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב יהודה is reading a פסוק to his son רב יצחק. When the son asks for a real-life example, the father names the son's own mother. This sets up the challenge in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: your youth (from the פסוק about the wife of your youth)

phrases.english: ...of your youth."
phrases.notes: This is the end of the פסוק in משלי ה:יח, 'rejoice with the wife of your youth,' which רב יהודה was reading to his son.

phrases.english: He said to him: Like whom?
He said to him: Like your mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: כְּגוֹן מַאן? אָמַר לוֹ: כְּגוֹן אִמָּךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the story begun in the lines before this section.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב יהודה names his wife as an example of the joyful 'wife of your youth.'

steps.title: But he also called her 'more bitter than death'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story. Another time, רב יהודה read his son a פסוק about a woman 'more bitter than death,' and when asked for an example, he also said: your mother.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But didn't רב יהודה read to his son רב יצחק: 'And I find more bitter than death the woman who is snares and nets'? His son asked him: Like whom? And he answered: Like your mother.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a contradiction. רב יהודה used the same woman as an example of a joyful wife and also of a woman 'more bitter than death.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both stories have the same structure: a פסוק, the question 'like whom?', and the answer 'your mother.' One praises her and one criticizes her, so how can both be true about the same person?

keyTerms.meaning: but isn't it that... (brings a contradicting source)
he read to him / taught him the פסוק

phrases.english: Is that so?
But didn't Rav Yehuda read
to Rav Yitzchak, his son:
"And I find more bitter than death

phrases.aramaic: אֶת הָאִשָּׁה אֲשֶׁר הִיא מְצוֹדִים וַחֲרָמִים״.
phrases.english: the woman who is snares and nets"?
And he said to him: Like whom?
And he said to him: Like your mother.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִינִי? וְהָא מַקְרֵי לֵיהּ רַב יְהוּדָה לְרַב יִצְחָק בְּרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 1 with a contradicting story about the same woman.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's praise of his wife as the joyful 'wife of your youth.'
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same person cannot be both a source of joy and 'more bitter than death,' yet רב יהודה named her for both.

steps.title: She gets angry easily but calms down with a word
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that both descriptions are true. She does flare up and is hard to deal with, which is the bitter side. But she is quickly calmed by a word, which is the joyful side.
steps.simpleTranslation: She does get very angry, but she lets it go with a single word.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by showing that both stories describe the same woman at different moments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Her quick temper explains 'more bitter than death.' Her readiness to make peace right away explains why she is still the wife who brings joy. There is no real contradiction, just two sides of one personality.

keyTerms.meaning: she is truly harsh / gets very angry
she lets it pass / gets over it

phrases.english: She does get very harsh,
but she lets it pass with a word.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Both statements are true about different sides of her character.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Calling her both joyful and bitter seemed contradictory.
steps.terutzMaskana: She is quick to anger, which is the bitter side, and quick to make peace, which is the joyful side.
steps.whatToRemember: רב יהודה's wife was both 'bitter' and the 'wife of your youth': quick to anger, but quick to be calmed.

steps.title: A woman truly bonds with her first husband
steps.stepSummary: רב שמואל בר אוניא, quoting רב, teaches that a woman is like unfinished material. She forms a true covenant only with the man who first 'made her a vessel,' meaning her first husband, as hinted in a פסוק from ישעיהו.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב שמואל בר אוניא said in the name of רב: A woman is like unfinished material, and she makes a covenant only with the one who made her into a vessel, as it says: 'For your husband is your Maker, ה׳ צבאות is His name.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new teaching about marriage. It says that a woman's deepest bond is with her first husband.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The image is of a craftsman: raw material becomes a finished vessel through the one who shapes it, so it belongs to him. The פסוק links 'your husband' (בֹעֲלַיִךְ) with 'your Maker' (עֹשַׂיִךְ), and the teaching reads this as the husband being the one who 'made' her.

keyTerms.meaning: unfinished raw material, not yet a complete vessel
makes a covenant / forms a true bond

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אוּנְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב:
phrases.english: Rav Shmuel bar Unya said in the name of Rav:
A woman is unfinished material,
and she makes a covenant
only with the one who made her into a vessel,
as it is said: "For your husband is your Maker,
the Lord of hosts is His name."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב שְׁמוּאֵל בַּר אוּנְיָא מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new teaching on the same broader theme of the bond between husband and wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman's true bond is only with her first husband, the one who 'made her a vessel.'

steps.title: A spouse's death is felt most by the other spouse
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that when a man dies, it is his wife who feels it most, and when a woman dies, it is her husband who feels it most.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: A man dies only to his wife, and a woman dies only to her husband.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא stating a general idea. This step gives the rule, and the next step gives its proofs.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Dies only to' means the loss is felt most sharply by the spouse. Others grieve too, but the deepest pain belongs to the husband or wife.
steps.confusionAlert: 'Dies only to his wife' does not mean nobody else mourns. It means the spouse feels the loss most of all.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: אֵין אִישׁ מֵת אֶלָּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ,
phrases.english: It was taught: A man dies only to his wife,
and a woman dies only to her husband.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: אֵין אִישׁ מֵת אֶלָּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another teaching on the closeness of husband and wife.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A death is felt most deeply by the surviving spouse.

steps.title: Proofs from אלימלך and רחל
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא proves both halves of its rule. אלימלך is called 'נעמי's husband' when he dies, and יעקב says 'רחל died on me,' showing that the loss belonged mainly to the spouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: A man dies only to his wife, as it says: 'And אלימלך, נעמי's husband, died.' And a woman dies only to her husband, as it says: 'And as for me, when I came from פדן, רחל died on me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא repeats each half of its rule and backs each one up with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק about אלימלך's death describes him by his relationship to נעמי, so the loss is framed as hers. יעקב says 'died on me,' speaking of רחל's death as his own personal loss.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא proves that a death hits the spouse hardest: אלימלך is 'נעמי's husband,' and רחל 'died on me' (יעקב).

phrases.aramaic: אֵין אִישׁ מֵת אֶלָּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
phrases.english: A man dies only to his wife, as it is said:
"And Elimelech, Naomi's husband, died."

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין אִשָּׁה מֵתָה אֶלָּא לְבַעְלָהּ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר:
phrases.english: And a woman dies only to her husband, as it is said:
"And as for me, when I came from Paddan,
Rachel died on me."
phrases.notes: בראשית מח:ז. These are יעקב's words to יוסף.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵין אִישׁ מֵת אֶלָּא לְאִשְׁתּוֹ, שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings פסוקים to support the rule in step 5.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that a death is felt most by the surviving spouse.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רות א:ג (Elimelech, Naomi's husband) and בראשית מח:ז (Rachel died on me).

steps.title: Three haircut schedules: מלך, כהן גדול, כהן הדיוט
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about not watching the king's haircut. It then brings a ברייתא with three haircut schedules.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'We do not see him (getting a haircut), etc.' The Rabbis taught: A king cuts his hair every day. A כהן גדול cuts it from Friday to Friday. An ordinary כהן cuts it once every thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns to a new line of the משנה, about the king's haircut. It quotes a ברייתא that sets up three different haircut rules, which the next steps will explain one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה mentioned the king's haircut, so the גמרא brings a ברייתא that expands on haircuts. The more public and important the person, the more often he cuts his hair. Each of the three rules will get its own source in the coming steps.

phrases.english: "We do not see him, etc."
phrases.notes: This quotes the משנה: no one may watch the king while he is getting his hair cut.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
A king cuts his hair every day,

phrases.aramaic: כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מֵעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת לְעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: a High Priest from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve,
an ordinary priest once every thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: מֶלֶךְ מִסְתַּפֵּר בְּכׇל יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic. It returns to the משנה after the earlier discussion about wives.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A מלך cuts his hair daily, a כהן גדול weekly, and a כהן הדיוט every thirty days.

steps.title: The king cuts daily so he looks beautiful
steps.stepSummary: The king's daily haircut comes from a פסוק saying people should see the king in his beauty.
steps.simpleTranslation: A king cuts his hair every day, as it says: 'Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the first rule of the ברייתא, the king's daily haircut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק says the people should see the king looking beautiful. Since the king is always seen in public, he has to keep up his appearance every day.

keyTerms.meaning: as it is said (introduces a פסוק)

phrases.english: A king cuts his hair every day,
as it says: "Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for the first rule of the ברייתא in step 7.
steps.raayaObject: The king cuts his hair every day.
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 33:17, "Your eyes shall see the king in his beauty."

steps.title: The כהן גדול cuts weekly because the משמרות change
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that the כהן גדול cuts his hair weekly because a new group of כהנים starts serving every week.
steps.simpleTranslation: The כהן גדול cuts from Shabbat eve to Shabbat eve. רב שמואל בר נחמן said in the name of רבי יוחנן: this is because the priestly shifts change.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second rule, the weekly haircut of the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a reason, not a פסוק. The כהנים served in weekly shifts called משמרות. Each week a new shift came in, so the כהן גדול freshened up his appearance to greet them.

keyTerms.meaning: the weekly shifts of כהנים serving in the מקדש
are renewed, a new one begins

phrases.english: A High Priest from Shabbat eve,
Rav Shmuel bar Nachman said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
Since the priestly shifts change.
phrases.notes: A new group of כהנים started its week of service each Shabbat eve, so the כהן גדול wanted to look his best for them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the king's rule to the כהן גדול's rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול cuts weekly because a new משמר begins every week.

steps.title: A כהן הדיוט learns thirty days from the נזיר
steps.stepSummary: The thirty days for a כהן הדיוט comes from a פסוק in יחזקאל, linked to נזיר through the shared word פרע.
steps.simpleTranslation: An ordinary כהן cuts once every thirty days, as it says: 'They shall not shave their heads, nor let their hair grow long; they shall only trim their heads.' We learn the word 'פרע' here from 'פרע' by a נזיר. Here it says, 'long hair they shall not grow,' and there it says, 'let the long hair of his head grow.' Just as there it is thirty days, so too here it is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source for the third rule. A כהן may not grow 'long hair,' and we find out how long 'long hair' is from the laws of נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same word פרע (long hair) appears for כהנים and for a נזיר, so the גמרא uses a גזירה שוה to connect them. A נזיר's growth period is thirty days, so 'long hair' means thirty days' growth. A כהן therefore has to cut before he reaches that point.

keyTerms.meaning: and he learns (one case from another)
learning one law from another because the same word appears in both
just as there, so too here

phrases.english: An ordinary priest once every thirty days,
as it is written:
"They shall not shave their heads,
and they shall not let their hair grow long;
they shall only trim their heads,"
and he learns "long hair" from "long hair" of a nazir.
It is written here: "long hair they shall not grow,"
and it is written there: "let the long hair of his head grow."
Just as there it is thirty,
so too here it is thirty.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source for the third rule of the ברייתא.
steps.raayaObject: An ordinary כהן must cut his hair every thirty days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: יחזקאל 44:20, linked by גזירה שוה to במדבר 6:5 (נזיר).
steps.confusionAlert: The thirty days does not come straight from the פסוק about כהנים. It comes from נזיר, and the shared word פרע is the bridge.

steps.title: A משנה confirms that a standard נזירות is thirty days
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא backs up the thirty days of נזיר with a משנה: a נזירות of no stated length lasts thirty days.
steps.simpleTranslation: And we also learned in a משנה: a נזירות with no set length is thirty days.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא supports the 'thirty days by נזיר' that the last step relied on, by quoting a משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גזירה שוה only works if נזיר really means thirty days. This משנה confirms that a נזירות of unstated length lasts thirty days.

keyTerms.meaning: and we also learned in a משנה
a נזירות taken without stating how long

phrases.english: And we also learned in a mishnah:
An unspecified naziriteship is thirty days.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּתְנַן נָמֵי: סְתַם נְזִירוּת שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the thirty-day נזיר period used in step 10.
steps.raayaObject: A standard נזיר period is thirty days.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in נזיר: סתם נזירות שלשים יום.

steps.title: Where do we learn thirty days for a נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source of the thirty-day rule for נזיר itself.
steps.simpleTranslation: And there, by נזיר, how do we know it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what source shows that a נזיר's period is thirty days. This sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We learned the כהן's rule from נזיר, and a משנה states the נזיר rule. But the משנה needs a source in the תורה too, so the גמרא asks for it.

keyTerms.meaning: from where do we know this?

phrases.english: And there, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the root source behind the נזיר rule used in steps 10 and 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה that a נזיר's period is thirty days.

steps.title: The word יהיה equals thirty
steps.stepSummary: רב מתנה answers that the פסוק says 'קדש יהיה,' and the word יהיה adds up to thirty.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מתנה said: because the פסוק says, 'He shall be holy.' The word יהיה adds up to thirty in גימטריא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question. The thirty days of נזיר comes from the number value of the word יהיה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In גימטריא each Hebrew letter has a number value: י is 10 and ה is 5, so יהיה equals 10+5+10+5 = 30. 'He shall be holy' is read as 'he is holy for thirty days.' This completes the chain from נזיר back to the כהן's haircut.

keyTerms.meaning: the number value of Hebrew letters

steps.whatToRemember: The full chain: a כהן cuts every thirty days, learned from נזיר through the word פרע. The נזיר's thirty days comes from יהיה = 30.

phrases.english: Rav Masna said:
Because the verse says: "He shall be holy,"
in gematria, it adds up to thirty.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מַתְנָה: דְּאָמַר קְרָא קָדֹשׁ יִהְיֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The word יהיה in 'קדש יהיה' has a גימטריא of thirty, which sets the נזיר period at thirty days.

steps.title: רב פפא asks why the כהנים should not shave completely
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא suggests that the פסוק might mean כהנים should not grow their hair at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said to אביי: Maybe the פסוק means the כהנים should not let their hair grow at all!
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא challenges the idea that כהנים may have some hair. He suggests that maybe they must keep their heads fully shaved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The source from יחזקאל says the כהנים must not let their hair grow long. רב פפא reads this as a total ban on growing any hair, which would contradict the idea of a thirty-day haircut.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said to Abaye:
Say that they should not grow [their hair] at all!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges how the יחזקאל פסוק (from step 10) should be read
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the פסוק allows some hair growth
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק could be understood as forbidding any hair growth at all

steps.title: אביי proves from the word order that some hair is allowed
steps.stepSummary: אביי shows that the פסוק allows some hair and only forbids letting it grow wild.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי answered: If the פסוק had said 'they shall not let long hair grow,' you would be right. But since it says 'and long hair, they shall not let grow,' it means some hair may grow, but they must not let it grow wild.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רב פפא from the exact wording of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק first mentions פרע (hair growth) and only then says what is forbidden. אביי reads this as permitting some growth while banning letting it grow out fully. That is why there is a set time for cutting it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: אִי כְּתִיב ״לֹא יְשַׁלֵּחוּ פֶּרַע״
phrases.english: He said to him: If it were written "they shall not let long hair grow"
it would be as you said;
now that it is written "and long hair [they shall not let grow]"
phrases.notes: The words in square brackets fill in the rest of the פסוק, יחזקאל 44:20.

phrases.english: there may be some hair growth,
but they should not let it grow out wild.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רב פפא's challenge
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of the פסוק's word order
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק bans any hair growth
steps.terutzMaskana: Some growth is allowed; only letting it grow wild is forbidden

steps.title: Should the haircut rule apply today too?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule comes from a פסוק, the כהנים should have to cut their hair even today.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, then nowadays too, the כהנים should have to cut their hair every thirty days!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short, sharp question: if this is a real rule from a פסוק, why don't כהנים keep it today?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the rule rests on a פסוק and is not just a practice for its time, it seems it should never stop. Yet כהנים today do not cut their hair every thirty days.

phrases.english: If so, nowadays too?
phrases.notes: He means: then today's כהנים should also have to cut their hair every thirty days.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on אביי's answer to raise a new difficulty
steps.kashyaTarget: The view that the haircut rule is a lasting rule from a פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule from a פסוק should still apply after the בית המקדש was destroyed

steps.title: Long hair is like wine: forbidden only when entering to serve
steps.stepSummary: Hair is compared to wine. Both are forbidden only when a כהן enters the בית המקדש.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is like wine. Wine is forbidden only when a כהן enters the בית המקדש, and allowed at other times. So too long hair is forbidden when entering, and allowed at other times.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the haircut rule only applies when a כהן comes in to serve. With no בית המקדש today, it does not apply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In יחזקאל, the ban on long hair appears right next to the ban on wine. The גמרא uses this to say both work the same way: they are tied to the time of serving. This explains why the rule is not kept today.

keyTerms.meaning: At the time of entering (the בית המקדש)

phrases.english: It is similar to wine:

phrases.aramaic: מָה יַיִן, בִּזְמַן בִּיאָה הוּא דְּאָסוּר,
phrases.english: just as wine is forbidden at the time of entering,
and permitted when it is not the time of entering,

phrases.aramaic: אַף פְּרוּעֵי רֹאשׁ, בִּזְמַן בִּיאָה אָסוּר,
phrases.english: so too long hair is forbidden at the time of entering,
and permitted when it is not the time of entering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of why the rule is not kept today
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The haircut rule applies at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: The haircut rule applies only at the time of entering the בית המקדש

steps.title: But the רבנן forbid wine even today
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי, explained by אביי, implies that the רבנן forbid כהנים to drink wine even today.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is wine really allowed when not entering? But a ברייתא teaches: רבי says, I say that כהנים are always forbidden to drink wine, but what can I do, since his repair is his ruin. And אביי said: Whose view do כהנים follow when they drink wine today? רבי's. This shows that the רבנן forbid it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the wine comparison. It brings proof that, according to the רבנן, wine is forbidden to כהנים even today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי says that כהנים today drink wine only because they follow רבי. That means the רבנן disagree and forbid it. If so, wine is not allowed outside the time of entering, and the comparison to hair falls apart.

keyTerms.meaning: But it was taught in a ברייתא

steps.confusionAlert: רבי is the one who is lenient here, not strict. He says that by right it should be forbidden, but in practice he allows it. The strict view belongs to the רבנן.

phrases.english: And is wine permitted when it is not the time of entering?
But it was taught: Rabbi says: I say:
Kohanim are forbidden to drink wine always,
but what can I do, since his repair is his ruin.
phrases.notes: He means that the same destruction that hurt the כהנים is what ends up allowing them to drink.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כְּמַאן שָׁתוּ כָּהֲנֵי חַמְרָא הָאִידָּנָא?
phrases.english: And Abaye said: According to whom do kohanim drink wine nowadays?
According to Rabbi. This implies that the Rabbis forbid it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the wine comparison used in step 17
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that wine is allowed when not entering the בית המקדש
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי's statement implies the רבנן forbid wine even today, so wine is not allowed outside the time of entering

steps.title: The רבנן forbid wine only because the בית המקדש may be rebuilt soon
steps.stepSummary: The רבנן's ban on wine today is a safeguard so that כהנים will be ready to serve, not a rule from the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: There, this is the reason: the בית המקדש may be rebuilt soon, and we need a כהן who is fit for the service, and there would not be one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the רבנן forbid wine today. Their reason has nothing to do with the basic rule from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the פסוק itself, wine is forbidden only when entering. The רבנן add a ban today for a separate reason: if the בית המקדש is suddenly rebuilt, a כהן must be ready to serve. So the comparison between hair and wine still works at the level of the פסוק.

phrases.english: There, this is the reason:
the Temple will soon be rebuilt,
and we need a kohen fit for the service, and there would be none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Defends the wine comparison against the challenge from רבי's ברייתא
steps.terutzResolutionType: Separating the basic rule from an added safeguard
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The רבנן hold that wine is forbidden by the basic rule at all times
steps.terutzMaskana: The רבנן forbid wine today only so that a כהן will be ready if the בית המקדש is rebuilt

steps.title: Then the same reason should apply to hair
steps.stepSummary: The safeguard reason for wine should also require כהנים to cut their hair today.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here too, I need a כהן fit for the service, and there would not be one!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא turns the answer back on itself. If the רבנן worry about readiness for wine, they should worry about it for hair too. Step 21 answers this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new reason, being ready for a rebuilt בית המקדש, fits hair just as well as wine. So the original question returns: why don't כהנים today cut their hair every thirty days?

phrases.english: Here too,
I need a kohen fit for the service, and there would be none.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the reason from step 19 to hair, bringing back the question from step 16
steps.kashyaTarget: The practice of not requiring haircuts for כהנים today
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The readiness reason for forbidding wine should equally require cutting hair today

steps.title: Hair can be fixed right away
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that hair is different from wine: a כהן with long hair can simply cut it and go right in.
steps.simpleTranslation: Here (with hair), it is possible for him to cut his hair and enter.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 20. It explains why the safeguard for wine does not also apply to hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The safeguard exists so a כהן will be ready to serve right away. A long-haired כהן can get ready in a moment by cutting his hair. So there is no need to make him keep it short all the time.

phrases.english: Here it is possible that he cuts his hair and enters.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 20
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction between the cases (hair can be fixed quickly)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The safeguard reason for wine should apply equally to hair.
steps.terutzMaskana: Hair can be fixed on the spot, so no safeguard is needed for it.

steps.title: Wine can also be fixed quickly
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pushes back: a כהן who drank wine can also sleep a little and go in, because רב אחא says a short walk or a little sleep removes the effect of wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: There too, it is possible for him to sleep a little and go in. As רב אחא says: walking a מיל or sleeping any amount takes away the effect of wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of step 21. It says wine can also be fixed quickly, just like hair.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the difference is "hair is easy to fix," then wine is easy to fix too. רב אחא teaches that a short walk or a little sleep sobers a person up. So the two cases look the same again.

keyTerms.meaning: Walking the distance of a מיל

phrases.english: There too it is possible
that he sleeps a little and enters,
as Rav Acha says:
Walking a mil, or sleeping any amount at all,
takes away the effect of the wine.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָתָם נָמֵי אֶפְשָׁר דְּנָיֵים פּוּרְתָּא וְעָיֵיל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 21
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only hair can be fixed quickly
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Based on רב אחא, wine can also be fixed quickly by a short walk or a little sleep, so the difference falls away.

steps.title: Sleep only helps for a small amount of wine
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב אחא's rule only works if the כהן drank up to a רביעית. If he drank more, walking tires him and sleep makes him even drunker.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it said about this: רב נחמן said in the name of רבה בר אבוה: they taught this only when he drank a רביעית. But if he drank more than a רביעית, walking will tire him all the more, and sleep will make him drunker.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the difference between hair and wine. It shows that wine cannot always be fixed quickly.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אחא's rule has a limit: it only works for up to a רביעית of wine. With more wine, a quick nap or walk does not help and can even make things worse. So wine still needs a safeguard, while hair, which can always be cut right away, does not.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it said about this?
A quarter-לוג, a set measure of liquid

steps.whatToRemember: Hair can always be fixed on the spot. Wine can only be fixed quickly if he drank a small amount. That is why the safeguard applies to wine and not to hair.

phrases.english: But wasn't it said about it:
phrases.notes: "It" means רב אחא's rule that a short walk or a little sleep removes the wine.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר אֲבוּהּ:
phrases.english: Rav Nachman said in the name of Rabba bar Avuh:
They taught this only
when he drank a quarter-log,
but if he drank more than a quarter-log,
walking will tire him all the more,
and sleep makes him drunker.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 22 by limiting רב אחא's rule
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the cited source
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Wine can always be fixed quickly, just like hair.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a small amount of wine can be fixed quickly. With more wine the כהן is not ready, so the safeguard is needed for wine.

steps.title: A drunk כהן ruins the service, a long-haired כהן does not
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי gives a different reason: a drunk כהן makes the עבודה invalid, so the רבנן made a safeguard for wine. A long-haired כהן does not make the עבודה invalid, so they made no safeguard for hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: כהנים who drank wine make the עבודה invalid, so the רבנן made a גזירה about them. כהנים with long hair do not make the עבודה invalid, so the רבנן did not make a גזירה about them.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי offers a new and different answer to the question of step 20. He explains why wine and hair are treated differently today.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference is no longer about how fast the problem can be fixed. It is about how serious the problem is. Since a drunk כהן ruins the עבודה, the רבנן guarded against it even today. Since long hair does not ruin it, they did not bother.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who gives a new answer here

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not adding to the earlier answer. He is giving a separate reason for the difference between wine and hair.

phrases.english: Rav Ashi said:
Those who drank wine, who make the service invalid,
the Rabbis made a decree about them;
those with long hair, who do not make the service invalid,
the Rabbis did not make a decree about them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a second answer to step 20, separate from steps 21-23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinction based on how serious each problem is
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The safeguard for wine should also apply to hair.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only wine invalidates the עבודה, so only wine received a גזירה.

steps.title: A ברייתא lists long hair next to wine for the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב אשי with a ברייתא that lists long-haired כהנים together with drunk כהנים as those who are liable to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: They challenged him: And these are the ones who are liable to death: those with long hair, and those who drank wine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to challenge רב אשי. The ברייתא treats long hair and wine as equally serious.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said long hair is less serious than wine, since it does not ruin the עבודה. But the ברייתא puts the two side by side as death-penalty sins. That seems to undercut his distinction.

keyTerms.meaning: They raised an objection (from a ברייתא or משנה)
Who are liable to death (at the hand of Heaven)

phrases.english: They raised an objection:
And these are the ones who are liable to death:
phrases.notes: This means death at the hand of Heaven, not a death sentence from a בית דין.

phrases.english: those with long hair, and those who drank wine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב אשי's distinction from step 24
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim that long hair is less serious than wine
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The ברייתא lists long hair right next to wine as a death-penalty sin, so they seem to be equally serious.

steps.title: Where do we learn the death penalty for long hair?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes that the death penalty for wine is written clearly in the פסוק, and asks where we learn the death penalty for long hair.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for those who drank wine, since it is written: "Do not drink wine or strong drink, you and your sons... so that you do not die." But for those with long hair, where do we learn it?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses to ask for the source of the ברייתא's ruling about long hair. It is setting up the next move, where it will find that source.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For wine, the פסוק itself says "so that you do not die." For long hair there is no clear פסוק that mentions death. So the גמרא asks where the ברייתא learned it.

keyTerms.meaning: From where do we know it?
So that you do not die

phrases.english: It makes sense for those who drank wine,
as it is written:
"Do not drink wine or strong drink,
you and your sons... so that you do not die."
But those with long hair, from where do we know it?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of the ברייתא quoted in step 25
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source in the תורה for the death penalty of a כהן with long hair

steps.title: Long hair is placed next to wine in the פסוקים
steps.stepSummary: The death penalty for a long-haired כהן comes from a comparison. In יחזקאל, the פסוק about long hair is right next to the פסוק about wine.
steps.simpleTranslation: Drunk כהנים and long-haired כהנים are compared to each other. It says: 'They shall not shave their heads, and long hair they shall not grow out,' and then it says: 'Neither shall they drink wine.' Just as drunk כהנים are liable to death, so too long-haired כהנים are liable to death.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question from step 26: where do we learn the death penalty for long hair? It comes from two פסוקים in יחזקאל that sit side by side.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The death penalty for wine is written clearly in the תורה. In יחזקאל, the ban on long hair comes right before the ban on wine. Because the two are placed together (a הֶקֵּשׁ), the death penalty carries over from wine to long hair.

keyTerms.meaning: Was compared. Two laws are placed side by side in the פסוקים, so they share rules (a הֶקֵּשׁ).
כהנים who let their hair grow long
Liable to death (death at the hand of Heaven)

phrases.english: Because those drunk on wine were compared to those with long hair.
It is written: "They shall not shave their heads,"
"and long hair they shall not grow out,"
And it is written: "Neither shall they drink wine, etc."
Just as those drunk on wine are liable to death,
so too those with long hair are liable to death.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question from step 26 about the source of the death penalty for long hair.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source of the death penalty for a long-haired כהן.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A הֶקֵּשׁ: in יחזקאל 44:20-21, long hair is placed next to wine, so it shares wine's death penalty.

steps.title: The same comparison should make long hair invalidate the עבודה
steps.stepSummary: If long hair is compared to wine for the death penalty, it should also be compared for making the עבודה invalid. That goes against רב אשי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And from this same comparison: just as drunk כהנים make the עבודה invalid, so too long-haired כהנים should make the עבודה invalid. This is a difficulty!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the comparison it just used and pushes it one step further. That goes against רב אשי's answer from step 24.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי said there was no safeguard for hair because long hair does not make the עבודה invalid. But if hair and wine are compared for the death penalty, the same comparison should also teach that long hair makes the עבודה invalid. The גמרא admits this is a real problem for now.

keyTerms.meaning: And from it, meaning from this very same source
Make the Temple service invalid (desecrate it)
It is a difficulty, a problem we cannot answer right now

phrases.english: And from it:
just as those drunk on wine make the service invalid,
so too those with long hair make the service invalid.
It is a difficulty!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the comparison from step 27 to attack רב אשי's distinction from step 24.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב אשי's claim (step 24) that a long-haired כהן does not make the עבודה invalid.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A comparison should carry over all the rules. If long hair shares wine's death penalty, it should also share wine's rule of making the עבודה invalid.

steps.title: רבינא asks who taught this law before יחזקאל
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי how a Torah law could come from יחזקאל's words. Who taught it before יחזקאל lived?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: This law, before יחזקאל came, who said it?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא challenges the whole idea of learning this law from פסוקים in יחזקאל. יחזקאל was a נביא, and a נביא cannot make a new Torah law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the law only comes from יחזקאל, then before he lived nobody knew it. That does not make sense for a law that should go back to the תורה. So how can the comparison in יחזקאל be the real source?

keyTerms.meaning: Until he came, meaning before he lived
The נביא whose ספר contains these פסוקים

phrases.english: Ravina said to Rav Ashi:
This law, until Ezekiel came,
who said it?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי הַאי עַד דְּלָא אֲתָא יְחֶזְקֵאל מַאן אַמְרַהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the source from step 27 itself: can a law really be learned from פסוקים in יחזקאל?
steps.kashyaTarget: The derivation in step 27 from the פסוקים in יחזקאל.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A Torah law must have existed before יחזקאל. So his ספר cannot be its true source.

steps.title: It was an old tradition, and יחזקאל attached it to a פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי points to a similar case taught by רב חסדא. The law was known by tradition all along, and יחזקאל only gave it a פסוק to lean on.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to your reasoning, what about what רב חסדא said: 'We did not learn this from the תורה of משה רבינו until יחזקאל came and taught us: Any foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh, shall not enter My Sanctuary to serve Me'? Before יחזקאל came, who said that? Rather, they knew it as a tradition, and יחזקאל came and attached it to a פסוק. Here too, they knew it as a tradition, and יחזקאל came and attached it to a פסוק.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי answers רבינא by showing that the same question applies to a known teaching of רב חסדא. He then gives one answer that works for both cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב חסדא also said a law was only found in יחזקאל. Since that law must have been kept before יחזקאל, it must have been a tradition passed down orally. In both cases, יחזקאל did not create the law. He only gave an existing tradition a פסוק to lean on.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning. It turns the asker's own logic back on him.
They learned it as a tradition passed down orally
He attached it to a פסוק, giving it support from the text

steps.whatToRemember: A law found in נביאים, like יחזקאל, can be an old tradition from סיני. The נביא only attached it to a פסוק.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,
this that Rav Chisda said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּבָר זֶה מִתּוֹרַת מֹשֶׁה רַבֵּינוּ לֹא לָמַדְנוּ,
phrases.english: This matter we did not learn from the Torah of Moshe our teacher,
until Ezekiel came and taught us:

phrases.aramaic: ״כׇּל בֶּן נֵכָר עֶרֶל לֵב וְעֶרֶל בָּשָׂר
phrases.english: "Any foreigner, uncircumcised in heart and uncircumcised in flesh,"
"shall not enter My Sanctuary to serve Me"

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּלֹא בָּא יְחֶזְקֵאל מַאן אַמְרַהּ?
phrases.english: until Ezekiel came, who said it?
Rather, they learned it as a tradition,
and Ezekiel came and attached it to a verse.
Here too, they learned it as a tradition,
and Ezekiel came and attached it to a verse.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's challenge from step 29 by comparing it to רב חסדא's teaching.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Parallel case (ולטעמיך), then a new idea: an oral tradition that was later supported by a פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The law about long hair started with יחזקאל, so nobody knew it before him.
steps.terutzMaskana: The law was an old oral tradition. יחזקאל only attached it to a פסוק.

steps.title: The tradition taught only the death penalty
steps.stepSummary: The tradition about long hair taught only the death penalty. It never taught that long hair makes the עבודה invalid, so רב אשי is safe after all.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when they learned this law by tradition, it was for the death penalty. That it makes the עבודה invalid, they did not learn.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא uses the idea from step 30 to answer the problem from step 28. This saves רב אשי's answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the law really comes from tradition, it includes only what the tradition taught, and the tradition taught only the death penalty. The side-by-side פסוקים in יחזקאל are just support, so we cannot use them to add the rule that the עבודה becomes invalid. So long hair still does not make the עבודה invalid, just as רב אשי said.

keyTerms.meaning: A law, here one passed down by tradition

steps.whatToRemember: A long-haired כהן is liable to death, but his עבודה is still valid. That is why the רבנן made a safeguard for wine but not for hair, as רב אשי said.
steps.confusionAlert: The word קַשְׁיָא in step 28 did not end the discussion. Here the גמרא answers that problem, and רב אשי's distinction stands.
steps.whyThisMatters: A tradition teaches exactly what it taught, nothing more. A פסוק used only as support cannot add new rules beyond the tradition.

phrases.english: And when they learned the law, it was for death;
that it makes the service invalid, they did not learn.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי גָמְרִי הֲלָכָה לְמִיתָה לְאַחוֹלֵי עֲבוֹדָה לָא גְּמִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the answer from step 30 to answer the קשיא from step 28 against רב אשי.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of a tradition
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Because of the comparison to wine, long hair should also make the עבודה invalid.
steps.terutzMaskana: The tradition taught only the death penalty. Long hair does not make the עבודה invalid, so רב אשי's answer stands.

steps.title: What does 'they shall trim their heads' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what כסום יכסמו את ראשיהם means. A ברייתא answers that it is a לוליינית haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is 'they shall trim their heads'? A ברייתא taught: a kind of לוליינית haircut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks what kind of haircut the פסוק in יחזקאל is describing. It answers with a ברייתא: a special haircut called לוליינית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוק that forbids long hair also tells the כהנים how to cut it. Now that we know they may not grow it long, we need to know what shape the haircut should be. The answer uses a new word, לוליינית, which the גמרא will explain next.

keyTerms.meaning: A לוליינית haircut, a special style of haircut

phrases.english: What is 'they shall trim their heads'?
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 44:20. It is the same פסוק that forbids the כהנים to grow long hair.

phrases.english: It was taught: like a kind of lulyanit haircut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the law about long hair to explaining the haircut the same פסוק describes.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What kind of haircut the words כסום יכסמו describe.

steps.title: What is a לוליינית haircut?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what לוליינית means. רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says it is a one-of-a-kind haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is a לוליינית haircut? רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: a unique haircut.
steps.whatsHappening: The word לוליינית is unclear, so the גמרא asks what it means. שמואל explains that it is a unique, special kind of haircut.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This answer tells us the haircut was not an ordinary one. It does not yet say what the haircut looked like, so the גמרא will ask again.

phrases.english: What is a lulyanit haircut?
Rav Yehuda said in the name of Shmuel:
A unique haircut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the unclear word used in the ברייתא from step 32.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the word לוליינית.

steps.title: What the special haircut looked like
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how this unique haircut actually looked. רב אשי says the tips of one row of hair lay next to the roots of the next row.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is it like? רב אשי said: the top of this one is next to the root of that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא wants a clear picture of the haircut. רב אשי describes it: the ends of one row of hair reach the roots of the next row.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Unique' was still too general, so now we get a real description. The hair was cut so neatly that each row's tips lined up with the base of the row beside it, making an even, layered look.

keyTerms.meaning: What is it like? How does it look?

steps.whatToRemember: The haircut the פסוק describes for the כהנים (כסום יכסמו) was a special, neatly layered style: the tips of each row of hair reached the roots of the next row.

phrases.english: What is it like?
Rav Ashi said:

phrases.aramaic: רֹאשׁוֹ שֶׁל זֶה בְּצַד עִיקָּרוֹ שֶׁל זֶה.
phrases.english: The top of this one is at the side of the root of that one.
phrases.notes: Think of rows of hair: the ends of one row lie right by the roots of the next row.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns שמואל's general word 'unique' into a concrete description.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the unique haircut actually looked like.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רב אשי: the tips of one row lie next to the roots of the next row.

steps.title: רבי points to בן אלעשה's haircut
steps.stepSummary: People asked רבי what the כהן גדול's haircut was. He told them to go look at בן אלעשה's haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: They asked רבי: What is the haircut of the כהן גדול? He said to them: Go out and see the haircut of בן אלעשה.
steps.whatsHappening: Someone asks רבי what the כהן גדול's haircut looked like. Instead of describing it, he sends them to see a real example on בן אלעשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This gives a living example of the haircut that the earlier steps described in words. Seeing it on a real person makes it clear in a way a description cannot.

keyTerms.meaning: A man who wore the כהן גדול's haircut

phrases.english: They asked Rabbi:
What is the haircut of the High Priest?
He said to them:

phrases.aramaic: צְאוּ וּרְאוּ מִתִּסְפּוֹרֶת שֶׁל בֶּן אֶלְעָשָׂה.
phrases.english: Go out and see from the haircut of ben Elasa.

steps.triggerLanguage: שָׁאֲלוּ אֶת רַבִּי: אֵיזֶהוּ תִּסְפּוֹרֶת שֶׁל כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a real-life example of the haircut described in steps 32-34.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What the כהן גדול's haircut looked like.

steps.title: Why בן אלעשה spent money on his haircut
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי: בן אלעשה spent his money for a reason, to show everyone the כהן גדול's haircut.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא: רבי says, בן אלעשה did not spend his money for nothing, but to show through himself the haircut of the כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: A ברייתא backs up what רבי said. בן אלעשה's expensive haircut had a purpose: to show people what the כהן גדול's haircut looked like.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Someone might think spending a lot on a fancy haircut is a waste. רבי says it was worth it, because it kept alive the knowledge of how the כהן גדול cut his hair.

keyTerms.meaning: It was taught in a ברייתא

phrases.english: It was taught: Rabbi says:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא עַל חִנָּם פִּיזֵּר בֶּן אֶלְעָשָׂה אֶת מְעוֹתָיו,
phrases.english: Not for nothing did ben Elasa spend his money,
but in order to show through him
the haircut of the High Priest.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא, רַבִּי אוֹמֵר: לֹא עַל חִנָּם פִּיזֵּר בֶּן אֶלְעָשָׂה אֶת מְעוֹתָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports רבי's answer in step 35 with a ברייתא explaining why בן אלעשה wore this haircut.
steps.raayaObject: That בן אלעשה's haircut really shows the כהן גדול's haircut.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing פרק כהן גדול
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא ends the second פרק of סנהדרין, called כהן גדול.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, כהן גדול.
steps.whatsHappening: This line closes the פרק. It is the traditional words said at the end of a פרק, saying we will come back to learn it again.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No new law is added here. It simply marks that the discussion of פרק כהן גדול is complete.

phrases.english: We will return to you, Kohen Gadol.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion of the כהן גדול's haircut.
